ComBat-refQL uses three complementary validation layers.

## Mathematical tests

Offline deterministic tests verify empirical-Bayes limits, exact contrast
parameterization, QL covariance against a one-degree-of-freedom edgeR test,
reference-centred dispersion identities, residual-information behavior,
model-consistent zero transport, numerical rollback, chunk equivalence, and
exact preservation of reference counts.

## Simulation with known truth

The factorial simulation independently varies mean batch effects, dispersion
multipliers, biological effects, replication, balance, overlap, library depth,
expression, gene dispersion, correlated modules, and outliers. It records
batch-effect bias and RMSE, dispersion-ratio recovery, biological-effect
preservation, transformation magnitude, count alignment, reference invariance,
runtime, and raw-count edgeR inference metrics.

The fast subset runs during development. The full run also evaluates pinned
ComBat-ref and ComBat-seq implementations. Results are tidy TSV files under
`validation/`.

## GFRN and NASA GeneLab data

The real-data workflows reproduce the count subsets used by the ComBat-ref
repository at pinned commit
`f0c6d3f313e9f1f29de2c8c8f12b98113443be55`. The GFRN analysis uses GFP
controls and HER2, EGFR, and KRAS perturbations across three batches. The NASA
analysis uses the public GeneLab liver count collection after excluding the
GLDS-168/RR1 stratum, matching the upstream analysis.

Both workflows compare unadjusted counts, ComBat-refQL, pinned ComBat-ref, and
pinned ComBat-seq. They report conditional batch association in leading PCs,
gene-level mean alignment, within-batch residual-dispersion alignment, and
reference invariance. These are empirical behavior metrics; simulations supply
truth-based recovery metrics.

See `validation/README.md` for commands and `validation/VALIDATION_REPORT.md`
for the recorded results.
